answer: Device-bound seating ties each agent to one hardware root key. The wharf registry admits a key once its manufacturer certificate verifies, then issues one non-transferable marble, the seat token. Every epoch a random timed challenge must be answered inside that enclave, so one box cannot serve two seats. A farm must buy a physical machine per head, with no sharing. A seat that misses one drops into karst status, unpaid until it re-proves. Honest agents need one machine; extracted chip keys are the known limit.
